prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct GradeScale and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Every bug here lives on a boundary, and boundaries are exactly what a casual test suite misses. Checking 85 -> B and 95 -> A passes all three broken implementations; it is 90, 80, 70 and 60 -- the first score in each band -- that separate >= from >, and 69 that exposes a missing band. The out-of-range values matter for the same reason: 101 and -1 are the only inputs where the validation either exists or does not. When a specification names a range, its endpoints are the test cases.
hints: Test the FIRST score in each band: 90, 80, 70, 60. A suite built from 85 and 95 certifies every broken implementation here.
Test 69 as well as 60 -- one implementation has no D band at all, and only a score inside that band reveals it.
The contract mentions scores below 0 and above 100. Those two inputs are the only ones that can catch missing validation.
